prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six openings place B045 first, but unanimity is not itself the argument. The scientific case is a complete discovery chain: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect (Holst, Drucker), identification of the active truncated GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), proof of insulinotropic and satiety action in humans, and then stable agonists that changed outcomes in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The mechanism is original and clear, independently confirmed by large outcome trials, and mature enough that recognition is timely. Rewarding the physiology and peptide discovery, with the drugs as the proof of its significance, keeps the prize on discovery rather than on industrial development.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Four names are credited but three seats exist. Mojsov's priority over the active peptide form is contested and Habener is outside the supplied names, so any trio can be argued to omit someone. Excluding Knudsen, who made liraglutide and semaglutide, risks looking like a prize that stops short of the therapy that made the discovery matter. I also recognise that the clinical scale of the drugs may be influencing how we perceive the originality of the underlying physiology.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks B045 first with Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, and treats Knudsen's contribution as largely industrial drug design with contested priority among the early peptide work.
responses.response: I agree on the trio and on the principle that a Nobel recognises discovery, but I would not dismiss Knudsen's work as merely industrial. Acylation to give a long half-life was a real conceptual step in turning a peptide with a two-minute half-life into a drug. My view is that it fits the citation as a consequence of the discovery and is better handled by wording the citation around physiology and the active peptide than by claiming it was irrelevant. I am less confident than Thomas that the Mojsov priority question is settled; it remains my main uncertainty.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks B045 first but proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, replacing Mojsov, and ranks optogenetics B006 second as a methodological invention of very broad use.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen swap seriously, since it rewards the clearest causal path to the drugs, but it would leave the identification of the active GLP-1 peptide uncredited and tilt the prize to a company programme. Five of six of us independently landed on Mojsov, which at least suggests that the discovery side is better supported. On optogenetics I partly disagree with ranking it second: the credit is spread across six names and a three-person prize would exclude Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, so I rank it below B003 and B015, where attribution is cleaner.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks B045 first, and B025 CAR-T second, arguing that engineered T cells are a new class of living therapeutics with strong clinical proof, while noting that Eshhar's early CAR concept is uncredited.
responses.response: I accept that CAR-T is a major new modality, but I rank it lower, at seventh. The gap in the credit is the issue for me: Eshhar's chimeric receptor is outside the supplied names, and Rosenberg's work is a different, TIL-based line, so a trio would blend two stories. The toxicity and solid-tumour limits also make recognition of the whole field somewhat early. I would keep it as a candidate for a later year rather than a prize now, and would not put it ahead of the HPV vaccine.

responses.point: Sandberg places the unfolded protein response B015 second, as an elegant and conceptually original ER-to-nucleus signalling mechanism, with a clean two-person credit of Walter and Mori.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution of B015 is cleaner than almost anything else on the shortlist, and the UPR is conceptually the most elegant. My hesitation is the weaker disease and therapeutic link compared with the HPV vaccine, which has cancer-incidence data. I would rank the UPR as a strong alternative rather than the preferred prize this year, and I would be willing to be persuaded if the committee prioritises mechanism over demonstrated patient benefit.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks the HPV vaccine B003 second as a clear, original discovery with population-level cancer prevention, noting the zur Hausen prize and the unresolved NCI versus Queensland priority issues.
responses.response: I largely share this view of B003, and I put it second as well. I would qualify the maturity point: the zur Hausen prize covered the viral aetiology, not VLP vaccine design, so I do not think it counts against novelty, but the Frazer and Zhou history and the parallel VLP work are real attribution risks that I cannot resolve from the supplied names. For that reason I treat B003 as the principal alternative rather than a candidate to share this year's prize with B045, which would also exceed three laureates.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's claim to the active GLP-1 peptide form outweighs Knudsen's development work for the third seat, and whether Habener or others outside the credited names have comparable claims.
Whether the committee wishes to reward discovery physiology alone or the translation to therapy within the same citation.
Whether the HPV priority questions (Frazer and Zhou, parallel VLP groups) can be settled well enough to make B003 a competitive alternative.
I have not independently verified priority details from primary documents.
statement.conflict_note: My profile documents about twenty co-authored works with committee colleague Thomas Perlmann, on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy; this is a research collaboration with no connection to any shortlisted candidate, so no recusal is needed, but I note it. I have a past Rockefeller link to Paul Greengard, who is not a candidate. No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from the provided profile.
